what_its_for: This medicine is used to treat cystic fibrosis (CF) in patients aged 6 years and older who have certain changes (mutations) in a gene called CFTR. It works by helping the CFTR protein in your body work better, which can improve lung function and reduce symptoms of CF such as breathing problems and frequent lung infections. Your doctor will confirm through genetic testing that this medicine is right for you.
how_to_take: Take tezacaftor/ivacaftor (the combination tablet) in the morning and ivacaftor alone (the evening tablet) about 12 hours later at night. Always take both tablets with food that contains fat, such as eggs, butter, peanut butter, cheese pizza, or whole milk dairy products. Swallow the tablets whole. Do not crush, chew, or break them. Try to take your doses at the same times every day to keep the medicine working steadily in your body.
dosing: The dose depends on your age and weight, and your doctor will determine the right dose for you. For adults and children 12 years and older, the usual dose is one tezacaftor 100 mg/ivacaftor 150 mg tablet in the morning AND one ivacaftor 150 mg tablet in the evening, approximately 12 hours apart. For children 6 to 11 years old, the dose is based on body weight and may be different. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions and never change your dose without talking to your doctor first.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose and it has been less than 6 hours since you were supposed to take it, take the missed dose as soon as you remember with fatty food. If it has been more than 6 hours, skip the missed dose and take your next scheduled dose at the regular time. Never take two doses at the same time or extra doses to make up for a missed one. If you are unsure what to do, call your pharmacist or doctor.
storage: Store this medicine at room temperature between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep the tablets in their original packaging or container. Keep the medicine away from heat, direct sunlight, and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not use the medicine after the expiration date printed on the package.
what_to_avoid: Avoid eating grapefruit or drinking grapefruit juice while taking this medicine, as it can increase the amount of medicine in your blood and raise your risk of side effects. Also avoid Seville oranges (often found in marmalade) for the same reason. Tell your doctor or pharmacist about ALL medicines, vitamins, and herbal supplements you take, because many drugs can interact with this medicine. This includes rifampin, St. John's Wort, certain antifungals (like ketoconazole or fluconazole), and certain antibiotics. Do not drink alcohol excessively. If you have liver problems, talk to your doctor before starting this medicine.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away if you experience any of the following: yellowing of your skin or the whites of your eyes, dark or tea-colored urine, stomach pain, or nausea and vomiting (these could be signs of liver problems); eye pain or changes in vision (this medicine can rarely affect the eyes, especially in children); rash, hives, or swelling of the face, lips, or throat (signs of an allergic reaction); unusual tiredness or weakness; high blood pressure. Also tell your doctor if your breathing problems worsen or you develop any new or unusual symptoms. Women who are pregnant or breastfeeding should consult their doctor before using this medicine.
when_it_works: You may start to notice improvements in your breathing and how you feel within a few weeks of starting treatment. However, it may take several months of consistent use to see the full benefit. Even if you feel better, do not stop taking this medicine without talking to your doctor first. This medicine is a long-term treatment and needs to be taken every day as prescribed to keep working.
special_populations: Children ages 6 to 11: Doses are lower and weight-based; follow your doctor's instructions carefully. Elderly patients: No dose adjustment is usually needed, but your doctor will monitor you closely. Liver problems: If you have moderate to severe liver disease, your doctor may lower your dose or this medicine may not be suitable for you. Kidney problems: No dose adjustment is typically needed for mild to moderate kidney disease, but tell your doctor about any kidney issues. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: It is not fully known if this medicine is safe during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Talk to your doctor right away if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding so you can weigh the benefits and risks together.
